title: Marusich v. Central Indiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC disposed of the complaint by returning the matter to Central Indiana Presbytery for a new BCO 31-2 investigation and report. It did not expressly answer either issue or state that the complaint was sustained.
first_summary: Marusich challenged Presbytery’s receipt of an investigative commission’s finding that accusations against a teaching elder did not establish a strong presumption of guilt, and the commission’s failure to provide minutes or a full report. The SJC returned the matter for a new BCO 31-2 investigation, requiring a narrative of the evidence and a recommendation for Presbytery’s consideration. It limited the decision to this case.
summary: Marusich challenged Presbytery’s receipt of a commission’s finding that accusations against a teaching elder did not establish a strong presumption of guilt, and the commission’s failure to provide minutes or a full report. Without answering either issue or identifying an error, the SJC remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation, a narrative of the evidence, and a recommendation for Presbytery’s consideration under regular orders. The decision expressly establishes no general rule for BCO 31-2 investigations.

sources.supports: Case identity, issues, remand instructions, case-specific limitation, and adoption by the full SJC.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 13–15 identify Case 2020-04 and the complaint; lines 88–90 state that the full SJC amended and adopted the panel decision, 17–4–0.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 60–65, printed p. 805, frame the two issues: receipt of the no-strong-presumption finding and failure to provide minutes or a full report.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 68–84, printed pp. 805–806, return the matter for a new investigation, narrative, recommendation, and Presbytery consideration. The majority gives no express issue answers or rationale.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Line 86, printed p. 806, limits the decision to this case and disclaims a general rule for every BCO 31-2 investigation.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No other decision is incorporated as the basis of judgment; lines 71–73 merely permit use of papers already in this case’s record. The later cited cases appear only in the dissent.

source_limits: The majority judgment is brief and does not identify the error supporting remand. The extensive dissent is not adopted reasoning.
